# Results — Study 927 (Dutch Auction) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Event set: **180** issuer
*modified Dutch auction* self-tender offers filed on SEC form **SC TO-I**, 2010-01-01 →
2025-12-31, harvested by one EDGAR full-text-search query (`q="modified Dutch auction"`,
`forms=SC TO-I`) and clustered per registrant; the event date is the **earliest SC TO-I
filing date** of each cluster — the offer's commencement, the day the tender documents
become public. **145** events on **109** distinct issuers survive the mechanical screens
(cached tape, ≥252 sessions before, ≥148 after, price ≥ $5). Abnormal return = issuer
**minus SPY**, both daily **total-return** closes (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`). One
execution lag throughout: the filing is public at the close of day *t*, the tradable leg is
entered at the close of *t+1*. As-of **2026-06-30** — data stamp as-of 2026-06-30.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n events | n issuers | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|--:|---|
| 128 issuer tapes + SPY (market) + BIL (cash) | 2010-06-18 → 2025-11-21 | 145 | 109 | Fingerprint `c39ea6c65ccb` |

**PROXY / ASSUMPTION.** Expiry dates are not in the EDGAR full-text index, so expiry is
proxied at **entry + 20 sessions** (Rule 14e-1's twenty-business-day statutory minimum).
Swept below. Transaction cost **10 bps one-way** per leg, charged on the day a slot is
opened and the day it is closed, **at the slot's real portfolio weight** — the sleeve is
equal-weight across live names, so an event sharing the book with two others is a third of
NAV and costs a third of a round trip. Booking a full-NAV round trip per event instead
would have overstated the drag by **1.55×** (the average number of live names) and let the
cost model, rather than the tape, carry the negative verdict; at their real weights the 145
events are **93.7** full-NAV round trips, a drag of 0.93 bps/day. The short-SPY leg pays
**30 bps/yr borrow**. Both swept. *Not* modelled: the intra-sleeve re-weighting turnover
when a name joins or leaves — second-order beside the open/close trips. The liquidity
screen uses a *second* cache of raw close × raw volume — approximate across splits, an
order-of-magnitude filter only.

**NAMED BIAS — the post-event survival screen.** The screens require **148 sessions of tape
after** the event (enough to close the six-month window), so an issuer acquired, taken
private or delisted within roughly seven months of its own tender is dropped. The direction
is knowable and it is not neutral: a self-tender is sometimes the opening move of a
going-private transaction, and a takeout is precisely the outcome that would print a large
positive six-month abnormal return. The screen therefore removes events that would push the
post-expiry drift **up**, which flatters this study's own "there is no drift" finding. Read
the drift result below as an upper bound on how empty it is.

## The four windows — where the money actually is

| Window | What it is | n | Mean | Median | *t* | Hit rate |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| (−5, −1) run-up | leakage / SC TO-C pre-announcement | 145 | **+1.44%** | +0.88% | **+3.20** | 58% |
| **Day 0** | the announcement repricing — **not tradable** | 145 | **+4.72%** | +3.26% | **+7.93** | **83%** |
| Tender window (*t+1* → expiry) | **the tradable leg** | 145 | **+0.12%** | +0.61% | **+0.17** | 55% |
| Expiry → +1 month | post-expiry drift | 145 | −0.25% | −1.08% | −0.29 | 43% |
| Expiry → +3 months | post-expiry drift | 145 | +1.69% | −0.28% | +0.88 | 50% |
| Expiry → +6 months | the "marks the bottom" claim | 145 | +2.76% | **−2.36%** | +0.71 | 47% |

The whole effect is one day wide. Day 0 is enormous and unmistakable; everything you could
act on afterwards is a coin flip, and at 6 months the **median** event is *below* SPY even
though the mean is above it — a handful of right-tail names carrying an otherwise flat set.

## Is the day-0 pop real? Four independent checks say yes

- **Jackknife.** Leave-one-out *t* stays in **[+7.81, +8.86]** — no single event drives it.
- **Block bootstrap** (5,000 draws, 5-event blocks): mean **+4.72%**, 95% CI
  **[+3.55%, +6.01%]**, 0.0% of resamples negative.
- **Placebo** (same 145 issuers, dates re-drawn at random on their own tapes, 2,000 draws):
  placebo mean **+0.01%** (sd 0.29%) against an observed **+4.72%** — **p = 0.0005**.
- **Date-locked.** Shifting the assumed event day destroys it almost entirely:

| Shift | −5 | −2 | −1 | **0** | +1 | +2 | +5 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Day-0 abnormal | −0.32% | +0.29% | +0.64% | **+4.72%** | +0.43% | −0.04% | +0.00% |
| *t* | −1.04 | +1.21 | **+2.51** | **+7.93** | +1.47 | −0.21 | +0.03 |

The small positive at −1 is the leakage the (−5, −1) run-up already measures.

## And the tradable legs? Nothing, by every test

- **Placebo p = 0.911** for the tender window and **p = 0.303** for the 6-month drift — the
  random-date control reproduces both effortlessly.
- **Bootstrap CIs straddle zero**: window **[−1.45%, +1.44%]** (41% of draws negative),
  6-month **[−4.55%, +11.95%]** (29% negative).
- **Jackknife**: window *t* ∈ [−0.04, +0.61], 6-month *t* ∈ [−0.12, +0.83].

## The calendar-time portfolio (the fix for overlapping events)

Long the issuer, short SPY, from *t+1* for 20 sessions, equal-weight across whichever names
are live (1.57 on an average live day; live on 1,847 of 4,046 sessions):

| | Mean/day | Sharpe | Vol | HAC *t* | Cumulative |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Gross | −1.23 bps | −0.169 | 18.4% | −0.63 | −54.2% |
| Net (10 bps, 30 bps/yr borrow) | −2.21 bps | **−0.302** | 18.5% | −1.14 | **−69.2%** |

## The long-only race — excess-of-cash vs excess-of-cash

Equal-weight long basket of live event names, parked in **BIL** when none is live, against
**SPY**; both minus BIL's actual total return:

| Arm | Excess-of-cash Sharpe | Mean/day | Vol | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Event basket, gross | +0.168 | +1.42 bps | 21.4% | +0.58 |
| Event basket, net (10 bps) | **+0.111** | +0.94 bps | 21.4% | +0.38 |
| SPY (charged the same one round trip) | **+0.809** | +5.50 bps | 17.1% | +3.60 |

Advantage (net basket − SPY): **−0.698** of excess-of-cash Sharpe. The HAC *t* on the daily
*mean* difference is **−2.00** — exactly on the two-sigma line, so read it as "the basket is
worse, and the tape is only just willing to say so at conventional size", not as a hard
rejection. The Sharpe gap itself is the load-bearing number, and it is wide: buying the
announcement one day late and holding through the tender window earns a fifth of the index's
risk-adjusted return while carrying a quarter more volatility.

## Robustness

**Era cut (split 2018-01-01).** The announcement effect is present in both halves; the
tradable legs are absent in both.

| Era | n | Day 0 (*t*) | Tender window (*t*) | 6m drift (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2010–2017 | 63 | **+3.10%** (+5.78) | +1.16% (+1.53) | −1.15% (−0.36) |
| 2018–2025 | 82 | **+5.97%** (+6.29) | −0.69% (−0.65) | +5.76% (+0.90) |

**Liquidity subset** (median 60-session dollar volume ≥ $10m before the event, n = 60): day
0 **+3.43%** (*t* = +4.88, hit 75%); window +0.14% (*t* = +0.13); 6m +0.78% (*t* = +0.24,
median **−2.89%**); calendar-time net Sharpe **−0.177**. Smaller pop on the names you can
actually trade — the classic size gradient — and still nothing tradable.

**Cost sweep** (one-way per leg, in and out). The window row is a **full-size single-name**
trade (all four legs on full NAV); the Sharpe row is the sleeve, where each slot is charged
at its real weight:

| One-way cost | 0 bps | 5 bps | 10 bps | 25 bps | 50 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Net tender-window return | +0.12% | −0.08% | −0.28% | −0.88% | −1.88% |
| Calendar-time net Sharpe | −0.176 | −0.239 | **−0.302** | −0.489 | −0.792 |

**Borrow sweep** (short-SPY leg, an assumption): Sharpe −0.295 / −0.302 / −0.320 / −0.369
at 0 / 30 / 100 / 300 bps/yr. Borrow is not what kills it — there was nothing to kill.

**Expiry-proxy sweep** (the 20-session assumption):

| Expiry | Window (*t*) | +1m (*t*) | +3m (*t*) | +6m (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| +15 td | +0.64% (+1.32) | −1.19% (−1.42) | +1.01% (+0.54) | +1.49% (+0.48) |
| **+20 td** | +0.12% (+0.17) | −0.25% (−0.29) | +1.69% (+0.88) | +2.76% (+0.71) |
| +25 td (n=144) | −0.38% (−0.49) | +0.01% (+0.01) | +2.08% (+1.15) | +2.89% (+0.85) |
| +30 td (n=144) | −0.16% (−0.17) | +0.11% (+0.15) | +1.42% (+0.74) | +1.96% (+0.64) |

No expiry assumption rescues a tradable edge.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports the stamp)

On a planted panel (145 synthetic issuers, one shared market factor, a **+470 bps**
announcement jump and **+300 bps** of six-month *log* drift):

- day 0: recovered **+468 bps**, *t* = **+23.06** — the jump, essentially exactly.
- six months: +300 bps of log drift is **+607 bps** of *expected simple buy-and-hold*
  abnormal return once the Jensen term (σ²/2, with 24% idiosyncratic vol over the half
  year) is carried; the harness recovers **+661 bps**, *t* = +2.74 — within a quarter of a
  standard error of the right answer.

On the pure null across 20 seeds, |*t*(day 0)| never exceeds **2.33** and clears 2 on
**2/20** seeds (roughly nominal), while |*t*(6m)| reaches **2.86** and clears 2 on
**7/20**. That last number is a **finding, not a bug**, and it comes from the same Jensen
term: a simple six-month buy-and-hold abnormal return is *right-skewed and positively
centred even under a null*, and the shared market factor makes those returns
**cross-sectionally correlated** on top. So the naive cross-event *t* at long horizons
over-rejects on the high side — exactly the Barber-Lyon / Kothari-Warner warning. The
correctly sized tests for the drift are therefore the **placebo** (which inherits the same
skew and correlation: *p* = 0.303) and the **calendar-time HAC *t*** (−1.14). Both say
nothing, and the real-tape six-month *t* of +0.71 is, if anything, flattered.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Mixed.** Two claims, two answers. The **announcement repricing is real and
  large**: +4.72% abnormal on the day the SC TO-I hits, *t* = +7.93, 83% of 145 events
  positive, placebo *p* = 0.0005, jackknife-stable, date-locked to a single session, present
  in **both** eras and in the liquid subset. The **"it marks the bottom" claim is absent**:
  the tradable tender window is +0.12% (*t* = +0.17, placebo *p* = 0.91) and the six-month
  post-expiry drift is +2.76% with a **−2.36% median** (*t* = +0.71, placebo *p* = 0.30, CI
  [−4.6%, +12.0%]). A genuine one-day repricing wrapped around a flat month and a flat half
  year. Named biases: the event set survives on SEC's **current** CIK→ticker map, so issuers
  acquired, taken private or liquidated after their tender are missing (survivorship); the
  screens additionally require 148 sessions of tape after the event, which drops any issuer
  taken out within ~7 months of its own tender — the very outcome that would have printed a
  big positive six-month drift, so the flat drift here is an **upper bound** on how flat it
  is; and the sample is the subset of self-tenders whose filings use the phrase "modified
  Dutch auction" (visibility).
- **Tradability — Mirage.** There is nothing to bank. Entering one session after the filing
  and holding to expiry earns +0.12% gross and **−0.28% net** at 10 bps on a full-size
  single-name trade; the calendar-time long/short sleeve compounds to **−69.2%** with a
  **−0.302** net Sharpe (and is already **−0.169** *gross*, so this is the tape's verdict,
  not the cost model's); and the long-only basket trails plain SPY by **0.70**
  excess-of-cash Sharpe, with a HAC *t* of **−2.00** on the daily mean difference — right on
  the two-sigma line, so the honest reading is a wide Sharpe gap that the mean-difference
  test only just calls at conventional size. The whole effect lives in a session you cannot
  be positioned for, and the drift the folklore promises is a right-tail illusion sitting on
  a negative median.
